issues.description: The problem statement and UML refer to a class named Meal (described as 'fully implemented') and all instructions/examples use Meal, but the template repository does not provide a Meal implementation. Instead the template contains an Order class with an identical shape to Meal and the template Main uses Order in its examples. This class-name/type mismatch (Meal vs Order) will confuse students: they will look for a ready-made Meal class as described in the problem, may not find it in the template, and will be unsure whether to implement Meal or to reuse Order. It also prevents a straightforward follow-up of the instructions and examples.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the template match the specification by providing a Meal class in the template (with the same constructor and getters as in the solution) and update example code to use Meal. Concretely: either (a) add template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Meal.java (copy or adapt the Meal implementation from the solution) and remove or rename the Order class to avoid duplicate/conflicting types, or (b) if Order is intended, update the problem statement and UML to refer consistently to Order instead of Meal. The first option (adding Meal and removing Order) is recommended to preserve the exercise text and examples.

issues.description: The problem statement consistently refers to a Meal class (e.g., 'Meal (Fully implemented)' and the UML showing class Meal), and the solution repository implements a Meal class. However, the template repository provides an Order class with the same shape (name and ingredients) instead of a Meal class. This naming mismatch (Meal vs Order) breaks the direct mapping from the problem description to the starter code: students looking for the Meal class described in the exercise will find Order.java in the template, causing confusion about which class to edit/use and increasing extraneous cognitive load.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the identifier consistent across artifacts. Update the template repository so it provides a Meal class matching the problem statement and solution: rename Order.java to Meal.java and change the class name from Order to Meal (constructor Meal(String, String[]), getters getName()/getIngredients()). Update any template references (e.g., Main) from Order to Meal. Alternatively, keep Order.java but add a Meal.java wrapper (or alias) that forwards to the same data, but the preferred fix is to use the single name 'Meal' consistently in problem, template, and solution.
